entries.embeddingText: organize friends into a mutual aid network, community care circle, local food system, shared pantry, community garden, food cooperative, buying club, produce exchange, neighbors helping neighbors
entries.answer: You want to turn a group of friends into a dependable mutual-aid network with stronger local food access. That crosses coordination, exchange, learning, and practical work, so Commonweave should hold the whole intention while each realm owns a clear piece. Start with one pilot people can actually maintain rather than designing the entire network at once.
entries.nextAction: Invite three to five people to a 45-minute mapping session where each person names one need, one offer, and one food project they would reliably help maintain.
subplans: Anarchadia: agree on participation, consent, responsibilities, and conflict handling.
FellowFare: map food sources, tools, transport, storage, offers, and needs.
Living School: identify growing, preserving, cooking, organizing, and food-safety knowledge gaps.
Cerbanimo: launch one pilot such as a shared pantry, garden plot, buying club, or produce exchange.

entries.embeddingText: learn to love myself, self-love, self-compassion, self-care, caring for myself before others, personal boundaries, consent, not being touched, clear intentions, clear peer communication, emotional capacity, relational safety
entries.answer: You are developing self-compassion alongside clearer physical and emotional boundaries. Living School can help you name your needs, recognize respectful consent, and practice communication that protects your capacity. Reflection is the beginning here, not the finish line.
entries.nextAction: Write one sentence describing how you want to treat yourself and one sentence stating a boundary you want trusted peers to understand.

entries.embeddingText: too many projects, overwhelmed, decide priorities, choose what deserves attention, coordinate multiple goals, plan next steps
entries.answer: You need a priority decision before you need another task list. Commonweave can compare the projects by urgency, dependency, energy, and visible payoff, then keep only one active lead intention.
entries.nextAction: List the projects and mark which one prevents harm, unlocks other work, or can show visible progress within seven days.

entries.embeddingText: learn, understand, study, practice, research, curriculum, lesson, gain knowledge, develop a skill, read results, watershed testing
entries.answer: This is primarily a learning intention. Living School should turn it into a short progression from explanation to guided practice to evidence that you can use the skill independently.
entries.nextAction: Name the real-world task you want to perform after learning, then gather one example you can practice on.

entries.embeddingText: build, repair, make, implement, code, design, skilled work, finish a project, greenhouse vent, prove work is complete
entries.answer: This belongs in Cerbanimo as a concrete skilled-work quest. The work should be split into a visible result, checkpoints, needed tools or knowledge, and proof that the result functions.
entries.nextAction: Define the smallest observable result that would count as done, then photograph or record the starting condition.

entries.embeddingText: obtain materials, borrow equipment, trade resources, buy supplies, sell offer need inventory delivery reclaimed boards trailer
entries.answer: This is a FellowFare exchange problem. Make the need specific, separate borrowing from permanent acquisition, and state the trust and return conditions before searching for matches.
entries.nextAction: Create one need card listing quantity, acceptable condition, pickup range, deadline, and what can be offered or guaranteed in return.

entries.embeddingText: community proposal, policy, voting, shared rules, collective decision, neighborhood approval, consent, governance, assembly
entries.answer: This is an Anarchadia governance question. The decision needs a clear scope, affected participants, consent threshold, objection path, and review date before anyone is asked to approve it.
entries.nextAction: Draft one sentence stating exactly what decision is being made and who is directly affected by it.

entries.embeddingText: organize a group, coordinate volunteers, create a community network, shared responsibilities, mutual aid governance, working together fairly
entries.answer: The group needs a lightweight agreement before it needs bureaucracy. Clarify the shared purpose, what participation actually asks of people, and how commitments can be changed without shame or hidden pressure.
entries.nextAction: Invite the first participants to confirm one shared purpose and one commitment they can realistically keep for four weeks.

entries.embeddingText: learn gardening, grow food, soil, seed starting, preservation, cooking, food safety, local agriculture knowledge
entries.answer: Living School can build the knowledge path around the exact food practice you plan to use, avoiding a sprawling agriculture curriculum that never reaches the soil.
entries.nextAction: Choose one crop or food practice and identify the next seasonal decision you must make correctly.

entries.embeddingText: build community garden beds, pantry shelves, compost system, greenhouse, irrigation, food storage, practical local food infrastructure
entries.answer: Cerbanimo should turn the food idea into a buildable pilot with a site, dimensions, materials, labor checkpoints, and a maintenance owner.
entries.nextAction: Choose one physical pilot and measure the actual space or capacity it must serve.
